blocks.text: Anaerobic respiration happens in many microorganisms and in some cells of higher plants. It also happens in the muscle cells of vertebrates. In anaerobic respiration, glucose is not completely oxidized. This type of respiration yields relatively small amount of energy from glucose molecule. As a result of anaerobic respiration, one glucose molecule yields only two ATPs (only about 2% of the energy present in glucose). The energy in two ATPs is equivalent to 14.6 kcal.
Anaerobic respiration consists of glycolysis followed by the reduction of pyruvic acid by NADH to either lactic acid or alcohol and CO₂ i.e., it may again be classified as;

a- Alcoholic Fermentation: In primitive prokaryotic cells (bacteria) and in some eukaryotic cells such as yeast, pyruvic acid is further broken down by alcoholic fermentation into alcohol (C₂H₅OH) and CO₂.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: Under alcoholic fermentation the book prints the lactic acid equation, 2(C₃H₄O₃) → 2(C₃H₆O₃), and labels its product “Ethyl alcohol”. Alcoholic fermentation gives ethyl alcohol and carbon dioxide: 2(C₃H₄O₃) + 4H → 2(C₂H₅OH) + 2CO₂ (the 4H come from 2 NADH).
b- Lactic acid Fermentation: In lactic acid fermentation, each pyruvic acid molecule is converted into lactic acid C₂H₆O₃ in the absence of oxygen gas.

blocks.title: Book correction
blocks.text: The formula of lactic acid is C₃H₆O₃, not C₂H₆O₃. Under lactic acid fermentation the book prints the alcoholic fermentation equation. Lactic acid fermentation releases no carbon dioxide: 2(C₃H₄O₃) + 4H → 2(C₃H₆O₃) (lactic acid).

This form of anaerobic respiration occurs in muscle cells of humans and other animals. It happens during extreme physical activities, when oxygen cannot be transported to the cells as rapidly as it is needed. Many bacteria also use lactic acid fermentation to get energy.

blocks.alt: Two rows. Top: glucose (six carbon beads) goes through Glycolysis, with 2 ADP + 2 Pi giving 2 ATP and 2 NAD+ giving 2 NADH, to 2 pyruvic acid; Alcoholic Fermentation, with 2 NADH + 2 H+ giving 2 NAD+ and 2 CO2 leaving, gives 2 ethanol (two carbons each). Bottom: the same glycolysis, then Lactic acid Fermentation, with 2 NADH + 2 H+ giving 2 NAD+, gives 2 lactic acid (three carbons each).
